what_happened: The dispatch description's transcript-layout claim (sibling ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/agent-*.jsonl files) does not match the live layout: subagent transcripts are nested at ~/.claude/projects/<slug>/<cc_session_id>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl with a sibling agent-<id>.meta.json (fields: agentType, description, toolUseId, spawnDepth). Confirmed empirically against this session's own project dir and cross-checked against context/project/memory/telemetry-guardrails.md's already-documented Tier 4 model, which matches the nested layout, not the dispatch's flat one. Corrected in the research report; no cost incurred since it was caught before any script was written against the wrong assumption.

Task 329 (the dependency this task's dispatch flagged for file-footprint serialization on scripts/orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh) is already [COMPLETED] and its issue-record.sh calls are already live in all three target arms (implemented/partial/failed-blocked). No serialization hazard remains; dispatch-metrics.sh calls can be added directly alongside the existing issue-record.sh calls in the same arms, following the exact same non-fatal invocation idiom.

Each dispatched subagent's own transcript (agent-<id>.jsonl) opens with a user-type line whose message.content is the literal dispatch prompt, which embeds the exact Context JSON block including task_number and dispatch_seq verbatim. This gives dispatch-metrics.sh an exact, unambiguous join from a postflight call site's own (task_number, dispatch_seq) to the correct subagents/agent-*.jsonl file -- no fuzzy timestamp-nearest or description-string matching needed.

The dispatch description asks for three postflight call sites (completion, partial, blocked), but orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh's dispatch_status case has seven arms, the whole case sits inside 'if have_outcome = true', and the partial) arm's existing issue-record.sh call is gated on partial_blocker_count -gt 0. Three arm-local calls would therefore miss research/plan dispatches, no-outcome dispatches, and every ordinary blocker-free partial -- contradicting the task's own 'one line per dispatch' acceptance bar. The plan resolves this with one call site sited after the case and before the per-task commit, recorded as Decision D2.

manifest.json's provides.context lists whole directories (so a new context/formats/*.md deploys automatically) but provides.scripts is an individual-file list. A new script not added there is silently never deployed, and deploy-root-guard.sh refuses source-store execution, so the script would appear completely dead with no error pointing at the cause. Also measured: a new context file needs its own index-entries.json entry with a line_count that validate-context-index.sh checks. Both made explicit plan tasks rather than left to discovery.

Phase 1 (format doc + index entry) landed clean on the first pass: the research-confirmed transcript join shape (nested subagents/agent-*.jsonl with escaped-string task_number/dispatch_seq matching) was verified live against this very dispatch's own transcript before writing the schema doc, so no rework was needed once Phase 2/3 code is written against it.

Phase 2's Scope Hypothesis (issue-record.sh at 394 lines, manifest.json issue-record.sh entry at line 109, flock append near lines 387-391) was re-measured before editing and matched exactly, so the skeleton's structural mirroring of issue-record.sh needed zero rework. Live deploy-tree verification (scratch task-dir append, no-tokens-key, deploy-root-guard refusal from source store) all passed on the first try.

The transcript join (Phase 3) was verified end-to-end against this dispatch's own LIVE transcript (agent-aad1158bea446f08d.jsonl) using a scratch 330_fake_slug task dir: real token counts, tool_calls, model, commits and churn all populated correctly on an exact task_number+dispatch_seq match, and tokens/tool_calls/model were correctly ABSENT (not zeroed) when dispatch_seq was deliberately wrong. No rework needed versus the research-confirmed join shape.

--backfill's commit-subject-grep selection (task N: / task N phase P:) does not account for task-number reuse after a vault operation: testing --backfill against task 329 live matched 20 commits, including an unrelated historical task that also used number 329 for a typst-primary doc update years earlier. The plan's Phase 4 Scope Hypothesis anticipated the dispatch-count-vs-events.jsonl mismatch risk but not this one. Worked around by not persisting the test output to the real task directory; documented as a known limitation in context/formats/dispatch-metrics.md is NOT yet done -- left open for a future task since it is out of this task's stated acceptance bar (which only requires backfilled:true + figure_provenance + omitted-not-zeroed on a completed task, all of which were satisfied).

Test fixture for the exact-match transcript join initially built message.content with pre-escaped backslash-quote/backslash-n sequences, producing a double-escaped string once jq --arg encoded it -- the real Claude Code transcript shape is a plain string with REAL quote/newline characters, escaped exactly once by the JSONL writer. Caught immediately by the (d.1) test itself failing with a correct-but-empty join result; fixed by writing real quotes/newlines directly into the bash heredoc-style variable.

All Phase 6 Scope Hypothesis line numbers (1708-line file, WORK (k) at 1386, WORK (i) at 1491, expected_dispatch_seq at 361-365) re-measured exactly as planned -- no drift despite the dependency task's own edits to this file. The existing 2452-line test-orchestrate-cycle-postflight.sh suite (166 cases) ran clean against the edited file with zero regressions, and a shellcheck diff against the pre-edit committed version showed zero new findings -- strong confirmation the WORK (m) insertion is side-effect-free for every other code path.

Acceptance evidence gathered using THIS task's own real commit history: --backfill 330, filtered to this round (recorded_at >= 2026-10-03), produced 8 real lines -- one per phase-commit -- with wall_clock_seconds in the 272-470s range for the six implementation-phase commits, three orders of magnitude above events.jsonl's 0.2-2.6s hook-runtime range, directly proving Acceptance 2. Acceptance 3 (blocked, and partial-with-zero-blockers) confirmed via direct dispatch-metrics.sh calls producing a line in both cases, matching the code-level proof that WORK (m) sits outside every arm-local gate.

verify-deploy.sh's whole-tree orphan detector flags tmp/noop-bash-count-<session-id>, a transient per-session marker written by detect-noop-bash.sh purely as a side effect of this dispatch's own interactive Bash tool use. Confirmed gitignored (matched by the blanket /.claude/ rule) and observed to appear/disappear across consecutive verify-deploy.sh runs within this same dispatch -- not caused by any committed file this task touches. Excluded in Phase 7's Reasoned Exclusions record rather than treated as a blocker.

run-all.sh's full suite sweep reports 3 pre-existing failing suites unrelated to this task: test-gate-out-repair-reporting.sh, test-lint-json-channel-discipline.sh (flagging the typst extension's chapter-quality-check.sh), and test-orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh. git log confirms all were last touched by unrelated tasks (326 phase 6, 250 phase 5/6), predating this dispatch. Excluded in Phase 7's Reasoned Exclusions record with the git-log evidence rather than attempted as an out-of-scope fix.

dispatch-metrics.sh introduces a flock-guarded .metrics.lock per task directory but metrics-lock was never registered as a runtime ephemeral-file class in scripts/lib/runtime-file-patterns.sh, so specs/330_per_dispatch_cost_and_timing_record/.metrics.lock is NOT gitignored and is now TRACKED in git (confirmed via git ls-files and git check-ignore). This diverges from the two sibling writers the script was explicitly modelled on: orchestrate-record-decision.sh had decisions-lock registered as the 20th class and issue-record.sh had issues-lock registered as the 21st. Remedy requires registering metrics-lock across runtime-file-patterns.sh's four parallel arrays plus its three block-copy consumers, regenerating the specs/.gitignore managed block via init-specs.sh, then git rm --cached the already-tracked lock file. Not hand-fixed here because it is a multi-file source-store change outside the orchestrator's postflight boundary.

Resolves the earlier open issue iss_1791080891215_ZQbD5d. metrics-lock is now registered as the 22nd ephemeral runtime-file class member across all six parallel arrays in runtime-file-patterns.sh plus both emitted gitignore blocks; the pinned fenced block in orchestrator-runtime-files.md was regenerated and re-verified byte-identical (test Case 3); the Case 5 member-count assertion moved 21 -> 22; the specs/.gitignore managed block was refreshed; and both already-tracked .metrics.lock files were untracked via git rm --cached without deletion. By the time of the fix the count had grown from one tracked lock file to two, confirming it recurred per dispatch rather than being a one-off. Verified: check-runtime-file-tracking.sh all three checks pass, test-runtime-file-tracking.sh 9/9, verify-deploy.sh 33/33.

test-verify-deploy-context-budget.sh resolves its config path against $HOME rather than the repository being tested: run from /home/benjamin/.config/nvim it exits 2 with 'expected /home/benjamin/agent-system/extensions/core/context/config/orchestrator-context-budget.json', a path that does not exist, while the real file sits at <repo>/agent-system/extensions/core/context/config/orchestrator-context-budget.json. The gate it guards (Gate 20, the orchestrator context budget lock) therefore cannot be exercised standalone from this repo; the budget figures had to be read out of the JSON by hand to confirm skill-orchestrate/SKILL.md had only 79 B of headroom. Same defect class as the open validate-state.sh omitted-argument default-resolution issue.

Closes the open --backfill task-number-reuse item by DOCUMENTING rather than re-engineering it, which the original entry itself named as the missing step ('documented as a known limitation in context/formats/dispatch-metrics.md is NOT yet done'). Added as Trap (d) in dispatch-metrics.md, promoting the section from three traps to four: it states the mechanism (commit-subject grep over a non-durable task number), the measured evidence (--backfill 329 matched 20 commits including an unrelated historical task that had reused the number), and three consequences -- derived figures from a backfill run are upper bounds, a backfill run's matched subjects must be checked before persisting into a task directory, and live postflight records are unaffected because they count commits by dispatch window with no grep involved. Deliberately NOT creating a task for a reuse-safe selection redesign: --backfill is a diagnostic convenience, live records carry the load-bearing figures and are unaffected, and figure_provenance already marks the affected figures derived rather than measured. Formally accepting a documented limitation is the proportionate resolution here.
